newsitem.title: GREECE: Bond trading thin, swaps ease in late dealing.
newsitem.headline: Bond trading thin, swaps ease in late dealing.

text.p: Greek forex forwards eased five to 10 basis points in late Thursday dealing and ecu/drachma was stable to easier around 305.42-47 because of foreign capital inflows, dealers said.
The central bank kept its intervention rate in overnight money unchanged at 11.90 percent.

The finance ministry auctioned 150 billion drachmas of three-year bonds, 100 billion of five-year bonds and 50 billion of seven-year bonds on Wednesday carrying coupons of 9.8, 9.2 and 8.9 percent respectively.
Selling commissions were set at 0.60 percent for the three-year bonds, 0.95 percent for the five-year bonds and 1.10 percent for the seven-year paper.
The ministry also accepted non-competitive bids of 45 billion drachmas in three-year bonds, 30 billion in five-year bonds and 15 billion in seven-year bonds.
Bids for all bonds were thin and prices of three- and five-year paper retreated further in late trade, a foreign bank bond dealer said.
"Three-year bonds are bid at 98.35 and five-year bonds at 97.35, below the auction's cutoff price. There is no trading in seven-year bonds," the dealer said.
The mark was quoted at 157.84/94 from Thursday's 157.885 fix, the dollar at 266.11/21 drachmas from 264.860 and the Ecu at 305.84/94 from 305.530 drachmas.
"Ecu/drachma is trading at 305.42-47, easier than in early Thursday dealings, on inflows from foreign investors," said a foreign bank forex dealer.
